assign.outcome:
**A `.md` file is a page now — link to it and it works.** `core/Page`s `child()` gained a fourth, last resort: after the `page.js` probe misses, it fetches `<url><name>.md` and renders a hit as a page — title from the first `# `, body through `md.file` (the fetch primes its cache, so one request, not two). `ext/markdown`s `md.resolve`/`md()` rewrite a link to a `.md` **beside the page you are on** into its route (`audit.md` -> `audit/`).

Proven headless: clicking the audit link on the css-audit task page lands on `/css-audit/audit/` with the report rendered (13 paragraphs, 0 raw text blocks, 1 fetch); a cold reload of that url renders identically; `/ext/Panel/doc/decisions/` made **zero** probes for `decisions/page.js`, so a declared note never reaches the fallback; `/ext/Panel/nope/` still 404s; the raw `.md` url still serves `200 text/markdown`. One `.md` link in the outcome before, one route after, and 0 of the 36 markdown anchors on that page still end in `.md`.

![](/framework/ai/2026-08-18/md-routes/md-route-click.png)

**Diverged from the brief, with numbers.** The brief asked for every same-origin `.md` link to be rewritten by path. Measured first: that turns **153 existing links into 404s** — 134 of them `ext/Doc` member files (`doc/method/append.md`) whose page is `api/<name>/`. So the rule shipped is *beside the page*, which is exactly what the sibling fallback can serve and therefore can never invent a dead url. Cost: `../doc/decisions.md` in a readme stays a raw link.

**Left, both outside the fence (one line each):** `ext/AITask/card.js:39` builds the `links:` pills as plain anchors, so **128** pill hrefs across the day board still point at raw `.md` — route them there, or write task `links` as `.../audit/`. And `ext/markdown/page.js` `methods:` should gain `route` (with `doc/method/route.md`) so the new method has an API page.
